messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PDR-91234 fired for service=autoscaler / symptom=queue_backlog (queue length > 75k)
pagerduty-bot: Incident PDR-91234 created and routed to #eng-oncall. Escalation policy: primary -> secondary.
alex_oncall: acked. pulling metrics now. anyone seeing user-facing 5xxs?
maria_eng: seeing increased 504s on hosted inference for a few customers, esp. embed-heavy workloads. logs show request queue growing.
jen_sre: grabbing cluster-scale metrics — autoscaler CPU/replica targets are at 72% but queue growth > 1000 req/s. looks like scaler loop is hitting rate limit on node provisioning.
alex_oncall: good context. impact = degraded tail latency for production embeddings, some timed-out requests. Sam from support, can you confirm customer impact?
sam_prod: Confirmed 3 major customers reporting intermittent timeouts. CS routing notes: some requests retrying but seeing elevated error rate. I'm pinging account owners.
alex_oncall: ok trying manual mitigation — bumping inference pool and temporarily diverting new traffic to a smaller model variant. will coordinate.
maria_eng: steps: 1) scale up dedicated pool nodes manually (k8s autoscaler blocked). 2) reduce max-batch-size on hot routes to avoid head-of-line blocking. 3) enable quick-fallback model variant for heavy requests.
alex_oncall: running manual scale command now:
```
kubectl --context=prod-nodes scale --replicas=24 deployment/inference-pool-hot -n redwood-serving
```
jen_sre: AWS API quotas showing a short burst limit hit, provisioning delayed ~6-7m. manual scaling will help if new nodes can join. also increasing pod spread to other AZs.
maria_eng: while nodes provision, apply config change to routing to prefer smaller-model variant for embed routes:
```
# temp route override
redwood route update --route embeds.v1 --model small-embed-quant --traffic 0.6
```
alex_oncall: applied route override, 60% traffic to small-embed-quant. monitoring.
sam_prod: telling customers we're mitigating and may route to smaller model; offering temporary quota increase.
jen_sre: nodes are attaching, new pods coming up (uid 7c9a). queue depth dropping but still elevated.
alex_oncall: reduced max-batch-size on hot workers:
```
kubectl patch deploy inference-hot --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"32"}]' -n redwood-serving
```
maria_eng: also toggled kvcache window to conservative mode to reduce memory pressure: `KV_CACHE_WINDOW=128` on hot path.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PDR-91234 acknowledged by alex_oncall at 1777777012.
alex_oncall: leaving notes in incident tracker. still watching latency. current p50/p95/p99 = 40ms / 380ms / 1.8s (was 2.7s).
sam_prod: customers on the thread reporting improvements for some requests. one large tenant still seeing bursts.
jen_sre: proposal: temporarily raise cluster node limit and enable fast-provisioning class for 10m to let remaining backlog drain. need approval from eng lead.
maria_eng: I approve the temporary fast-provisioning — triggering now and will revert after backlog drain.
alex_oncall: done. also we should add a throttle rule to stop accepting huge batched jobs from internal test clusters (they're skewing metrics).
support_lead: I've notified affected customers with ETA ~10-15m. prepping an incident update to share with execs.
jen_sre: backlog cleared to <4k at 1777777280. autoscaler telemetry shows it missed two scale-up windows due to API rate limiting; filed follow-up ticket to add quota-aware logic.
alex_oncall: nice. removing route override and rolling back manual batch-size change after 5m stable.
maria_eng: leaving follow-up actions: 1) add autoscaler retry/backoff for cloud API quota errors, 2) add circuit-breaker to reject oversized single-batch requests when queue > 50k, 3) improve alert to include provisioning delays.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PDR-91234 resolved by alex_oncall at 1777777384.
alex_oncall: incident resolved, leaving full notes in the incident doc. handing off to maria for postmortem. tagging action owners @maria_eng @jen_sre @eng-sre. :white_check_mark:
